text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwe government has built a Z$6 million double-storey mansion for First Lady Grace Mugabe in Harare's upmarket Borrowdale district. The mansion, which is almost complete, was built by the Ministry of Construction and National Housing under a scheme meant to benefit senior civil servants.

- Zimbabwe commercial banks have suspended interest payments on foreign currency accounts due to the central Reserve Bank's new requirements on statutory reserve deposits which were announced last month.
- Zimbabwe is tightening screws on multinational companies accused of evading tax through transfer and under-pricing, according to local acting commissioner of taxes Gershem Pasi.

- German companies who attended a Zimbabwe trade/investment promotion conference in Hamburg last month have plans to invest over Z$500 million in the southern African state in fields such as mining, tourism, manufacturing and horticulture.

- The Zimbabwe high court has nullified -- for the second time in a year -- mayoral polls in the country's southern town of Masvingo on grounds municipal authorities had illegally barred other candidates and given victory to a candidate from President Robert Mugabe's ruling ZANU-PF party.
